etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English organizen, organysen, partly from Middle French organiser and partly from its etymon, Medieval Latin organizō, from Latin organum (“organ”); see organ.

quote.citation: 2015, Vladimir S. Lerner, “The impulse observations of random process generate information binding reversible micro and irreversible macro processes in Observer: regularities, limitations, and conditions of self-creation”, in arXiv‎[1]:
quote.text: Multiple bits moving in macroprocess join triplet macrounits which logically organize information networks encoding units in structures enclosing triplet code.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To constitute in parts, each having a special function, act, office, or relation; to systematize.

quote.text: This original and supreme will organizes the government.

quote.citation: 2003, Rodney Castleden, King Arthur: The Truth Behind the Legend:
quote.text: With Arthur it was clearly the Falklands factor writ large. Actions such as organizing and building the Wansdyke or Cadbury 11 (the refortification) would have strengthened the authority and extended the power of whichever king was the organizer.

quote.citation: 2008 April 18, Susan Dominus, “Young, Hip and Wild About Comic Books”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: Ms. Crabapple did a lot of posing in bikinis, and less, to pay her way through F.I.T.; in addition to showing in fine art galleries and drawing comics, she organizes events she calls Dr. Sketchy’s, a life drawing class that’s also a burlesque show with music, costumes and seminudity.

definitions.definition: (transitive, chiefly used in the past participle) To furnish with organs; to give an organic structure to; to endow with capacity for the functions of life

quote.citation: 1691, John Ray, The Wisdom of God Manifested in the Works of the Creation. […], London:  […]  Samuel Smith, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: These nobler faculties in the mind of man,  […]  matter organized could never produce.

quote.citation: 1828, Thomas Busby, A Complete Dictionary of Music:
quote.text: Formerly , those Catholic priests who sung in parts : so to sing , was to organize

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To band together into a group or union that can bargain and act collectively; to unionize.
